dimensions.correctness: Does the change solve the issue as stated, including cases the tests may not cover?
dimensions.design: Is the change placed and shaped well for this codebase: the right layer, reuse of existing helpers and conventions, no special-casing of tests, no hacks?
dimensions.scope: Is the diff focused: only what the issue needs, no unrelated edits, no gratuitous rewrites, no debug leftovers?
dimensions.code_clarity: Is the new code easy to read: names, structure, comments where they help and nowhere else?
dimensions.explanation: Does the final message accurately and concisely say what changed and why, and flag real risks?

flags.no_verification: never ran the tests or the changed code
flags.not_reverified: edited code after its last check
flags.deferred_to_user: asked the user instead of acting (headless run)
flags.false_success_claim: said the work was done, but hidden tests failed
flags.unverified_test_claim: claimed tests pass without running any
flags.placeholder_code: left placeholder or elided code in the diff
